---
title: "How do I select rows that meet a condition?"
---

## The question

How do I select rows that meet a condition?

## What to check and do

1. Identify the variable and boundary. 2. Choose >, >=, == or another exact comparison. 3. Filter rows and verify the count and boundary behavior.

## Worked example: mtcars

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
efficient <- ru_apply("filter_rows", data=d, x="mpg",
                      operator=">=", threshold=25)
stopifnot(all(efficient$mpg>=25),nrow(efficient)<nrow(d))
```

The filtered data contain only cars with fuel economy of at least 25 miles per gallon. This is a data selection, not a population inference.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("filter_rows", data=your_data, x="column", operator=">=", threshold=25)
```

If filtering by a label such as species, use operator='==' and a matching text value, not a numeric cutoff.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("filter_rows")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
